notes.r171_atp_synthase_gpr_evidence: AND members are the subunits whose loss is taken to close the reaction: ATP6/8/9 (mtDNA) and the nine nuclear core subunits (alpha, beta, gamma, delta, OSCP, b, d, h, f). Subunits e, g, k are dimer-specific and the Y. lipolytica monomer lacking them is catalytically active (Hahn 2016, PMID 27373333); g and k were not found in the purified Y. lipolytica enzyme (Liu 2015, PMID 25759169); S. cerevisiae e, g, k are not required for an enzymatically active ATP synthase (Arnold 1998, PMID 9857174); the S. cerevisiae subunit-j null keeps about half the ATPase activity (Vaillier 1999, PMID 9867878). OR-rule review 2026-10-29, REPORT section 7.1.
notes.r171_atp_synthase_gpr_evidence_tier: literature on the Y. lipolytica enzyme (structure, purified-enzyme composition, hydrolysis rather than synthesis) and S. cerevisiae mutants; no Y. lipolytica knockout of e, g, k or j; keep-or-drop of j is a judgement

YALI1B28025g.reason: a single accessory subunit has no evidence of catalysing ATP synthesis alone; dimer-specific (Hahn 2016), not found in the purified Y. lipolytica enzyme (Liu 2015)

YALI1B15733g.reason: as g; not found in the purified Y. lipolytica enzyme (Liu 2015)

YALI1E38131g.reason: dimer-specific; the Y. lipolytica monomer lacking e, g, k hydrolyses ATP at about the rate of the dimer (Hahn 2016); S. cerevisiae e, g, k not required for an enzymatically active ATP synthase (Arnold 1998)
